news.title: Vote now for your Chelsea August Goal of the Month winner!
news.body_en: Several memorable Chelsea strikes were scored in August, and we are asking Blues supporters to vote for their favourite in our first Goal of the Month vote of the season. The new campaign has started well for our men's side under Xabi Alonso. Premier League victories have been recorded over Fulham and Brighton and Hove Albion, while Luton Town were defeated in the Carabao Cup second round. Nine goals have been scored along the way – and many have been shortlisted in our August Goal of the Month vote. There is also representation from our Academy sides, with special strikes from those featuring for Cobham Next Gen and our Under-18s. The vote is now open on the Chelsea Official App, and supporters can watch each of the nominated goals below before having their say. McGillvary gets a Goal of the Month nomination with his first for our Under-18s. The schoolboy gave the Blues a lead after six minutes against Birmingham, and we raced away to a 4-1 victory. What a first goal it was from McGillvary, who steadied himself and arrowed a shot into the top corner from outside the box. The Brazilian gave us the perfect start inside the first 33 seconds of our season. There was little danger when a Fulham clearance was sent into the Chelsea half, but Maxence Lacroix won his header and the ball broke to Palmer, who deftly flicked it into Joao Pedro's path. He took a touch before finishing coolly over Bernd Leno. This was a well-worked team move which showcased the fluidity of our football under Alonso. Centre-back Lacroix was found in the Fulham penalty area by Palmer, and he tricked his way past Jorge Cuenca and crossed from the byline. Rogers arrived perfectly and swept home to net on his Chelsea debut. Our 3-2 victory at Craven Cottage was secured in the second half by Palmer. Rogers flicked a header on to Joao Pedro, who bound into the Fulham half, waited for an overlap from the England international and slipped in his fellow attacker. Cole assessed his options and opted to guide a shot between the goalkeeper's legs. A dramatic comeback by Cobham Next Gen against senior opposition secured a 2-2 draw, and was followed by a penalty shootout victory. The Blues were kicked into life in the game by Bettoni, who provided a neat first-time finish after Sol Gordon drove to the byline and cut the ball back for his team-mate. This was the first of three goals Pennie scored to get his hat-trick at Cobham against the Royals. The striker showed his strength to hold a defender at arm’s length before smashing a shot into the top corner. Heze Grimwade gets plenty of credit too for threading a defence-splitting pass into Pennie's path. Neto pounced to put us two goals ahead inside the first 15 minutes of our first home Premier League fixture of the season. Rogers was the creator, collecting a Joao Pedro knock-down and forcing his way past Mario Vuskovic. The England international squared the ball and Neto burst forward to finish beyond Bart Verbruggen. Joao Pedro, given a less-than-friendly reception by the fans of his former club Brighton, briefly silenced the away end with a deserved goal. Jorrel Hato was instrumental, exchanging passes in our half with Rogers and surging upfield. The Dutchman eventually fed the ball to Joao Pedro and the Blues' No.9 made no mistake with his finish. Our third nomination from the Brighton win and second for Cole, just like his first, was the match winner. It was also yet another example of our front three combining incisively, as Joao Pedro controlled and laid off a throw-in for Palmer to collect. The latter advanced 20 yards and then curled a shot expertly beyond Verbruggen. Richards played his part in a stunning fightback by the Blues, who came from three goals down on the brink of half-time to triumph 5-4 in a thrilling match. Richards netted our second goal as we built momentum. Reggie Watson and Bettoni had already had efforts blocked, but there was no stopping Richards' follow-up, as he smashed his shot into the back of the net.

news.title: Chelsea Women vs Aston Villa: How to watch, kick-off time, live stream info
news.body_en: Chelsea Women play at Stamford Bridge for the first time since making it our permanent home on Saturday lunch time as we kick off our Women's Super League campaign for the 2026/27 season against Aston Villa. Having secured our qualification for this season's UEFA Women's Champions League with a 6-2 aggregate win over Real Sociedad, thoughts quickly turn to our domestic curtain-raiser at Stamford Bridge. The Blues will play all of our WSL fixtures at our new permanent home from this season onwards, beginning with Saturday's lunch-time game against Villa. Here is everything you need to know about how to watch Chelsea Women against Aston Villa, including kick-off time and how to follow the action on official Chelsea channels. Chelsea Women's game against Aston Villa takes place on Saturday 5 September 2026 at Stamford Bridge, with kick-off scheduled for 12.35pm UK time. Tickets are still available to purchase for Saturday's match, but if you can't make it to Stamford Bridge, then you can watch the match live on BBC One, BBC iPlayer and the BBC Sport website in the UK. As always, team news, live updates and match coverage will be provided in our Chelsea Women vs Aston Villa Women Match Centre on the Chelsea Official App and Chelsea website. You can also follow along via Chelsea Women’s social media channels on X, Facebook, Instagram and TikTok. The Blues go into the match having won back-to-back games against Real Sociedad in our Women's Champions League qualifying third round tie, by an aggregate score of 6-2. Meanwhile, Aston Villa come into the new season after a difficult start to 2026. Only relegated Leicester City (zero) won fewer points in the WSL during 2026 than Aston Villa did with their tally of seven. The Villans’ average of 0.6 points per game this year is their worst on record in the Women’s Super League in a calendar year. Chelsea have won all 12 of our Women’s Super League meetings with Aston Villa. Despite losing 4-3, Aston Villa scored more goals in their most recent WSL game against Chelsea, in March, than in their prior 11 league meetings with the Blues (two goals). That was also the first game in Women’s Super League history in which both teams scored three first-half goals. In the away meeting last season, Chelsea won 3-1 with goals from Aggie Beever-Jones, Keira Walsh and Sam Kerr. Be there to welcome CFCW to our new home at Stamford Bridge when we take on Aston Villa in our first Women's Super League match of the season on 5 September at 12.35pm!

news.body_en: The draw for the league phase of this season's UEFA Women's Champions League takes place on Friday, with the Blues set to learn our next opponents in European competition. Sonia Bompastor's side completed the job in the third qualifying round of the Women's Champions League with a 1-0 win away at Real Sociedad on Wednesday evening, thanks to Keira Walsh's second-half goal. That gave us a 6-2 victory over the Spaniards on aggregate and put our name in the hat for the next stage of the competition. Here is everything you need to know ahead of the draw for the league phase of the UEFA Women's Champions League. The draw takes place at 11am UK time (12pm CET) on Friday 4 September. The draw will be streamed live on UEFA.com and the official UEFA Women's Champions League app and will last around 45 minutes. The draw takes place at the House of European Football in Nyon, Switzerland. Nine teams qualified automatically for the league phase and are joined by nine clubs, including Chelsea, who entered via the third qualifying round play-off ties. Under the format introduced last season, teams face fixtures against six different sides in the league phase, playing half of those matches at home and half of them away. The 18 participating teams will be split into three pots based on their individual club coefficient ranking, with Chelsea among the top seeds in Pot 1. Each team will then be drawn to play two opponents from each of the three pots, playing one match against a team from each pot at home and one away. In principle, teams from the same association cannot be drawn against each other, and each team may play against a maximum of two opponents from any other one association, although UEFA reserves the right to adapt this rule in case of deadlock situations or any other relevant constraints. There are 18 teams competing at this stage of the competition. The Blues will face two sides from each of the three pots below, but clubs from the same association are kept apart at this stage. news.title: Denner signs for Chelsea
news.body_en: Chelsea is pleased to confirm the signing of Denner from Brazilian side Corinthians, with the full-back signing a contract until 2034. Denner, whose full name is Denner Alves Evangelista Pereira, has joined up with the Chelsea CNG squad. The 18-year-old is a forward-thinking, left-sided defender who rose through the youth ranks at his hometown club and last year starred as Corinthians Under-20s finished runners-up in the prestigious Copa São Paulo de Futebol Júnior cup. He scored three goals and provided two assists throughout the competition, including the opener in the final with Sao Paulo. Denner is a Brazil youth international and was a member of their Under-17 side that won the South American Championships in 2025.

news.title: UWCL Highlights: Real Sociedad 0-1 Chelsea

'I want to make Stamford Bridge a fortress'

UWCL Full Match: Real Sociedad vs Chelsea
Sonia Bompastor hails Blues youngsters after Champions League qualification
news.body_en: Sonia Bompastor praised Real Sociedad’s resolve after our 1-0 win in San Sebastian on Wednesday night and was happy to have the opportunity to feature some of our younger players. Added to our 5-2 win over the Spanish side at Plough Lane last week, we qualified for the Women’s Champions League with a 6-2 aggregate victory. Chelsea Academy graduate Lexi Potter started the match, while fellow Academy star Chloe Sarwie was introduced in place of Sandy Baltimore. New 18-year-old signing Nelly Las also came off the bench. With only two games played, we have already achieved a key objective in our season, and Bompastor was keen to praise the efforts of her team. ‘I'm pleased with the result,’ she said afterwards. ‘We kept a clean sheet, which is always important, and when you do that, you always have a bigger chance to win games. I'm glad we could rotate the team with the starting XI, but also the players who came in. ‘I think today we gave some really good opportunities to the young players to come and experience a Champions League game, so when you have the opportunity to do that, I think it's always something really positive. ‘I'm happy and really excited now to be in the Champions League this season. The goal was for us to qualify, which is what we have done. ‘People will probably think when you are Chelsea, it’s easy to do, but we played against a really strong team in Real Sociedad. Over the two legs, they showed some really good quality, and I think these two games are a really good preparation for us to come into the season in the league.’ The Blues will now return to Cobham, recover and prepare for our first WSL match of the season against Aston Villa on Saturday. Bompastor is hoping for a bumper crowd to cheer her side on as we mark the first game at Stamford Bridge since we made it our permanent home. ‘First, it's time to focus on recovering from the game,’ she continued. ‘We are really excited to come into the WSL game on Saturday against Aston Villa. Playing at Stamford Bridge will also be something really special. ‘We are really excited to start the league on Saturday at home, in front of all our fans. I can't wait to be in that moment. ‘I'm hoping for the fans to show up and to come and support us. We will need their support. It will be an important game because we want to begin strongly and start with a win against Aston Villa.’ This Saturday, Chelsea will play at Stamford Bridge for the first time since it became our permanent home. Welcome the Blues by securing your ticket for our first WSL clash of the season against Aston Villa now!

news.title: Match Report: Real Sociedad 0-1 Chelsea (2-6 on agg.)
news.body_en: Chelsea will be in Friday's draw for the league phase of the UEFA Women's Champions League after securing a 1-0 win over Real Sociedad at the Estadio Zubieta on Wednesday evening, putting them through with a 6-2 aggregate score. On a hot day in San Sebastian, the Blues kicked off looking to build upon our 5-2 win from Plough Lane the week before. The first half saw the two sides battle against each other with Chelsea in firm control of possession. The second period began with intensity. An Aggie Beever-Jones shot was palmed away by goalkeeper Julia Arrula, and from the resulting corner, the ball fell to Keira Walsh well outside the box, and the England international took the opportunity to hit the shot to put Chelsea 1-0 up and four goals ahead overall. The contest was a tight one, and our Spanish opponents once again proved that they are a force to be reckoned with. Yet the work had been largely done in the final 20 minutes of the first game, setting us up to take a three-goal advantage into this fixture. Sonia Bompastor made four alterations to her starting lineup following our 5-2 victory over the Spanish side at Plough Lane last week, bringing Lucy Bronze, Kadeisha Buchanan, Wieke Kaptein and Lexi Potter onto the XI for the return leg. The match began as it had on home turf: with Real Sociedad keeping the Blues at bay with their well-organised setup. It took 18 minutes for the first real chance of the game when Lauren James released Ellie Carpenter down the right with an insightful pass, but the Australian had her cross intercepted before it could reach Beever-Jones in the middle of the penalty area. James and Carpenter combined again a few minutes later to pick out Walsh, and the midfielder was able to get the shot away, but the ball rolled comfortably into the goalkeeper's arms. There was then some brief danger up at the other end of the pitch when Sociedad's Ava Seelenfreund burst through into the box, but a smart recovery tackle from Naomi Girma stopped the striker in her tracks. Yet the advantage was firmly with Chelsea as we put pressure on the home side, Carpenter getting round the full-back again after almost half an hour and forcing the goalkeeper to get down quickly to make the save. Half-time saw midfielder Giulia Dragoni make her competitive debut for the Blues as she came on in exchange for James after the break. There was a sharper attacking intent from Chelsea, and we soon made the breakthrough when Beever-Jones forced a good save, and Walsh hit one of her trademark shots from range beyond the goalkeeper from the resulting corner. The four-goal overall deficit spurred the home side on to throw caution to the wind. Ainhoa Marin, who scored in the first leg, went close before Kadeisha Buchanan was called upon to make a key tackle inside the box to prevent another chance. Naomi Girma then headed clear a further chance from the home side's fourth corner inside the space of two minutes. Sociedad's competitiveness really made things tough for Chelsea, and although we were restricted in terms of clear-cut chances, there were plenty of positives to take from the evening. Substitutes Alyssa Thompson and Maika Hamano caused plenty of problems with their movement up front, while Nelly Las gave a good account of herself as she also made her competitive debut for the Blues. This was by no means a classic Chelsea performance, but the most important factor was to get the job done and we did so with professionalism and control. After the first leg, Sociedad could've gone all out in attack to reduce the deficit, but they stayed true to themselves as they worked hard to keep us from extending the lead even further. We now head into Saturday's WSL clash with Aston Villa at Stamford Bridge knowing that we have already secured an important objective with only two games played. We will now compete in this season's Women's Champions League, beginning with the league phase. Chelsea are through to the league phase, and we will discover our opponents on Friday when the draw is made in Nyon. We take on Aston Villa in the Women's Super League at Stamford Bridge on Saturday at 12.35pm and you can still secure your tickets by clicking here! news.title: Kiano Dyer completes loan switch

news.title: Chelsea FC Women announces new business leadership roles
news.body_en: Chelsea FC Women is pleased to announce the appointments of Nadia Shahrestani as Chief Operating Officer and Giulia Mazzia as Chief Revenue Officer. Both have played a significant part in shaping the growth of CFCW and these newly created roles, which they have progressed into, reflect the scale and ambition of the club as we enter a new era. They will continue to report into the CEO of CFCW, Aki Mandhar. Shahrestani has worked at Chelsea for 20 years, including across almost every part of CFCW, helping build the club from the ground up. Most recently, she has played a key role in our move to Stamford Bridge, strengthening player safeguarding and developing new opportunities for our fans. As she begins her new appointment, she says: ‘I've watched this club grow and establish itself as one of the best in the world, on and off the pitch, and I am immensely proud to help shape what comes next. ‘From how we run our matchdays at Stamford Bridge and Plough Lane, to how we protect and support our players and fans, and how we continue to champion the growth of the sport we love — it means everything. This is just the beginning of what we can achieve.’ Mazzia has led our commercial team through significant revenue growth, helping redefine what is commercially possible for the women’s game. Under her leadership, CFCW has secured a series of industry-first partnerships, helping create new opportunities for our athletes, fans and the club. She says: ‘At CFCW, we challenge ourselves to think differently and find partnerships and commercial opportunities that don’t just generate revenue, but strengthen what we’re building as a club and add to the experience of our fans and players. I believe getting that balance right is fundamental to building a business that is both ambitious and sustainable, and ultimately reflects the quality and potential of what happens on the pitch.’ The new era begins on Saturday with every home WSL game to be played at Stamford Bridge – kicking off with Chelsea vs Aston Villa. news.title: Naomi Girma on her 'goal' against Real Sociedad and second leg expectations
news.body_en: Last week’s 5-2 win over Real Sociedad saw defender Naomi Girma named Blues captain for the evening, and she marked the occasion by scoring a crucial equaliser after the Spanish side had taken an early lead. Or did she? Girma was officially credited with the goal by UEFA, but speaking ahead of the second leg in San Sebastian, she revealed that what looked to be a header from a dangerous inswinging Katie McCabe corner wasn’t what it seemed. ‘So… I didn't actually touch the ball on the goal,’ Girma confirmed straight away. ‘It was Katie's goal. Yeah, we all went and celebrated with her. ‘It’s always an honour to wear the armband because we have such a great team and such great players. It’s also great because you know that everyone on the team is a leader and leads during the game too.’ Sociedad started strongly and gave the Blues a real test at Plough Lane. The teams went in at half-time with the scores locked at 1-1. After the break, we inched ahead thanks to a Veerle Buurman header, but our determined opponents fought back once more as we passed the hour mark at 2-2. The final portion of the game saw us burst into life with a brace from Melvine Malard and a Lauren James strike, handing us a three-goal advantage in the second leg. Girma explained how we made the final breakthrough, but also warned against complacency in the second leg. ‘We were able to wear them down throughout the game,’ she said. ‘And I think we did a good job of capitalising on our opportunities, especially near the end, to get those three goals in the last part of the game. There was a lot of good play. I think we just started expressing ourselves and playing free. ‘They're a really good side. I think we know nothing's given and you have to earn everything going into every game. ‘I think they'll be aggressive. They'll be disciplined again but obviously trying to get forward to score goals. As you saw in the first game, they are a good side and they were really good in their defence and good at creating opportunities when they could. I think they'll be looking to do that again. ‘So we're going to have to come out and put in a good performance. That’s definitely been the messaging throughout the team and that's what we're hoping to do tomorrow.’ This season has seen Chelsea face back-to-back Women’s Champions League qualifiers against Real Sociedad before the start of the Women’s Super League campaign. We will return to our new permanent home at Stamford Bridge for the first league fixture against Aston Villa this Saturday with two competitive fixtures already in the bag. It’s a different way to start the season than we have been used to at Chelsea and, while it would’ve been preferable to qualify automatically for the UWCL, Girma feels it could give us the edge against Villa. ‘Playing two Champions League games at the beginning of the season is definitely different than I've experienced since being here,’ Girma concluded. ‘In pre-season we did our best to prepare, knowing that these were going to be our first games. So we did have this in mind. ‘Hopefully it sets us up well for the season to have played two competitive matches already. The Champions League is a big goal of ours. We’ve known from the end of last season that this is something we were going to have to do. ‘The preparation in pre-season has been leading up to this. It's been really good.’ This Saturday, Chelsea will play at Stamford Bridge for the first time since it became our permanent home. news.title: Shumaira Mheuka signs new Chelsea contract and joins Celtic on loan

news.title: Jorrel Hato on a strong start, our dangerous connection and Arsenal test
news.body_en: Jorrel Hato declared Chelsea’s first mission of the season – securing a 100 per cent record from our opening three matches – as complete but is already eyeing the next step forward for the team against Arsenal this Sunday. The Dutchman has featured in every game under Xabi Alonso thus far, starting our Premier League wins over Fulham and Brighton & Hove Albion at left wing-back and coming off the bench as we beat Luton Town in the Carabao Cup. Those games all ended in victory; the most recent being our 4-3 win against Brighton at Stamford Bridge on Sunday. It was a game which could have gone more smoothly for the Blues, but as Hato makes clear, three points is three points, especially at this stage of the season. ‘It was a bit crazy,’ he said. ‘We scored a lot of goals and, of course, we're happy with the win, but we conceded three goals and I think that's something we can work on. ‘But, of course, if you concede three and you score four, you win the game. So, I'm happy about that. ‘It still matters, I think, because you want to win 4-0, not 4-3. But still, what I said is, if they score three and you score four, you did a good job.’ Hato got the assist for our third goal against Brighton, but it was the attacking contribution of our front three of Cole Palmer, Joao Pedro and Morgan Rogers which again caught the eye in the final third. That trio has nine goal contributions between them in our opening two league games. ‘I think they can find each other really well; they have a great connection,’ Hato added. ‘It's very important to have those guys up front. I think we are very dangerous with attackers on the bench as well, so that's something positive. ‘There's a lot of movement when we have the ball, runs in behind, coming into the ball. I think the connection between those three, and with me and Pedro [Neto] on the side, I think we did a great job.’ So far so good for the Blues, then, but next up comes another challenge as we travel away to title holders Arsenal in the Premier League for a 4.30pm kick-off on Sunday. ‘We look at things game by game,’ the defender concluded. ‘I think we had a great start. We spoke with each other and said: "Okay, the first week, three games has to be three wins," and we did that. So now we're looking forward to Arsenal. ‘I can't see the future, but we try to improve to not concede three goals, but we know we are very dangerous up front, that we will score goals. ‘I think against Arsenal is a good test, but I think it was against Fulham and Brighton as well. They are both great teams and we won those games, so we are looking forward to the next one now.’

news.title: Joao Pedro analysis: Why the Blues' master of all trades stands alone in 2026
news.body_en: Since the start of 2026, no Premier League player has scored more goals in all competitions than Joao Pedro As he begins his second full season in Blue, the Brazilian has made himself at home at the centre of Chelsea’s attack. And what a start he has made to the new campaign. The 24-year-old registered a goal and an assist in our opening weekend win over Fulham at Craven Cottage, and repeated the feat in our first outing at Stamford Bridge: a 4-3 victory over Brighton and Hove Albion. That takes Joao Pedro’s Premier League goals tally for Chelsea to 17, just two shy of what he managed in two seasons at Brighton. But look at his contribution across all competitions and the figures are even more impressive. Since the beginning of 2026, no Premier League player can better Joao Pedro’s 15 goals in all competitions – and his strikes against Fulham and Brighton suggest he shows no signs of slowing down any time soon. His performance against Brighton in our first home league game of 2026/27 was arguably one of his best yet for the Blues, as he topped stats tables across the board and was voted by supporters on the Chelsea Official App as our Player of the Match. A versatile forward when he arrived at Stamford Bridge, Joao Pedro has increasingly been used as the central striker in the Blues’ attack, currently spearheading an exciting front three alongside Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers in the early stages of Xabi Alonso’s reign. That has seen Joao Pedro’s goalscoring instincts come to the fore as a penalty box predator, with all but one of his 15 goals in 2026 coming from inside the area – his stunning UEFA Champions League strike away at Napoli back in January the one exception. There has been a ruthless efficiency to his game too: his 25 goals for the Blues better his expected goals total of 22.4, and he is averaging a goal every 162 minutes, better than one goal every two games. When looking at the chances he has had compared to the goals he has scored, it gets even better, with a shot conversion rate of 22 per cent. Of his 115 attempted shots, 52 per cent have found the target, and of those 55 per cent have ended up in the back of the net. It is not just his finishing that has been so impressive; his all-round game has been leading the way for Chelsea since he arrived at Stamford Bridge. With assists factored in, Joao Pedro has 33 goal contributions in his 54 appearances for the Blues. The next best of our current squad are Pedro Neto and Palmer, with 21 goal contributions each during the same period. Neto is also the only Chelsea player who can better Joao Pedro’s 66 completed dribbles, while there is athleticism and physicality to go with the silky skills and precise finishing. The Brazilian also tops our charts for duels won – 296 – 33 more than second-placed Moises Caicedo – and no current Chelsea player can match his 102 aerial duels won since the start of last season. A true master of all trades then, but it's Joao Pedro’s prolific form in front of goal that continues to catch the eye in 2026.

news.title: Romeo Lavia on how Xabi Alonso is trying to find that extra one per cent
news.body_en: Romeo Lavia is feeling great. But best of all for Blues fans, the midfielder believes he is going to get even better with the support of his team-mates and new manager. The 22-year-old has now started both Premier League games under manager Xabi Alonso and is enjoying making an impact on the pitch, something he did from the off last Sunday when he tapped home his first Chelsea goal to open the scoring against Brighton as the Blues won 4-3 at the Bridge. Having made it two wins in two in the league, Lavia highlighted the Blues’ developing mentality, which he believes is making the difference. ‘Our mentality has been great so far, starting from pre-season,’ Romeo opened. ‘And the manager has really been big on that to help us get that extra per cent to help us get the three points on the weekend. So far, it's been great. ‘It's all about building confidence. Obviously, my team-mates are giving me a lot of it, and the manager as well. It's just about building game by game, and I feel great, so hopefully it can continue forever.’ Even the cool, calm and collected Lavia couldn’t hide his joy after scoring his first for Chelsea, admitting he might have the video on loop! He continued: ‘It means a lot to score my first – a lot. I’m very happy – to score at the Bridge as well. For a first one, it can't get any better. I think I'm going to rewatch the goal a few more times. It's not the best-looking goal, but I'll take it every day. ‘It was a fantastic reaction from the fans, and from my team-mates as well. I really felt the love, so it was an amazing feeling.’ In a game that saw the visitors peg the Blues back, Lavia recognises the group will only get better in time, with all eyes on our trip to the Emirates this weekend, where we’ll go head-to-head with London rivals Arsenal. ‘We know our colleagues, and when we know that our colleagues can take over, we just need to make sure the rest goes with it,’ he added. ‘We realise that it's automatic – that we just push each other. We know our colleagues will take over in the end. It's honestly a great group to be in, and the demands in training every single day make it easier to then perform on the weekend. ‘There's a lot of work that goes behind the scenes, and it was just about putting that into practice. And we're happy that they came off well [against Brighton], so I’m very happy.’

news.title: PGA South League report: Chelsea Women’s Under-18s 6-1 Crystal Palace Under-21s
news.body_en: Chelsea Women’s Under-18s made it three wins from three so far this season with a 6-1 victory over Crystal Palace Under-21s. Chelsea Women's Under-18s, who play in the PGA Under-21 Women's League, took the lead through captain Keira Johnson before an own goal doubled our advantage. Palace pulled one back, but Gabi Storey struck just before half-time to send the Blues into the break 3-1 ahead. Carla Gardiner, Aysia Matabaro and substitute Annie Boichat added further goals after the interval. Leanne Champ’s side created plenty of chances and worked hard defensively when required to continue our positive start to the campaign. Chelsea’s patience in possession was rewarded after 19 minutes. The ball was worked around the back line to Sophie Leach, whose pass through the Palace shape found Storey. The midfielder turned and lifted the ball over the defence for Matabaro, who beat her marker to reach the byline and pulled a cross back for the arriving Johnson to power home first time. Sadie Gregory replaced Emelia Addison a minute later and Chelsea doubled the lead on 34 minutes after another well-worked move. Quick passing moved the visitors out of position, allowing Leach to find Johnson between the lines. They combined to release Maisie Brickell on the right, and she took a positive first touch towards goal before skipping past two defenders. Her cross took a deflection off a Palace defender and reached the goalkeeper, who spilled the ball over the line for an own goal. Palace reduced the deficit five minutes later, capitalising on a transition in Chelsea’s defensive half, but the Blues restored our two-goal cushion before the interval. Brickell and Matabaro combined down the right in the 44th minute and, although the visitors defended Matabaro’s shot well, Chelsea’s midfield reacted quickly to regain possession. Storey collected the ball on the edge of the box, shifted it out of her feet and struck from 20 yards, sending her effort across goal and into the bottom corner. Champ made three changes at half-time, with Zoe Ciccardini, Tess Finn and Jahyma Putman replacing Elise Christian, Storey and Chelsea N’Drin. Ciccardini was involved as Chelsea added a fourth eight minutes after the restart. She won the first contact from a Palace throw-in, and Johnson gathered the loose ball centrally before spotting Gardiner’s run between the two centre-backs. Johnson’s pass released the forward, who showed composure as the goalkeeper rushed off her line and dived at her feet. Gardiner took the ball around her and passed into the empty net. Matabaro added our fifth on 67 minutes at the end of another flowing move. Ciccardini took a quick throw-in down the left to Matabaro, who turned as Chelsea worked the ball back around to Finn. Finn played forward to Rebekah Pierce on the edge of the box, and she combined with Johnson to find Brickell out wide. Another dangerous delivery across the box picked out Matabaro, who finished first time. Boichat replaced Gardiner in the same minute and needed just eight minutes to add her name to the scoresheet. Chelsea were awarded a free-kick down the side of the penalty area, and Brickell floated her delivery over the wall towards the players waiting at the far post. Boichat met it with a header that struck the crossbar and went in to complete the scoring. The result continues Chelsea’s winning start to the Professional Game Academy South League season. After two matches, the Blues have six points, with 14 goals scored and just one conceded. Chelsea travel to Southampton for our next Professional Game Academy South League fixture on Wednesday 2 September. We then head to Swindon Town in the Women’s National League Cup on Sunday 6 September. news.title: Sonia Bompastor delivers injury update on Blues quartet
news.body_en: Chelsea head coach Sonia Bompastor has provided updates on the fitness of Nathalie Bjorn, Erin Cuthbert, Manaka Matsukubo and Mayra Ramirez ahead of our UEFA Women's Champions League third qualifying round second leg against Real Sociedad. A place in the league phase of the competition can be secured tomorrow evening at the Estadio Zubieta, and the Blues have travelled to the Basque Country with a commanding 5-2 advantage after the first leg at Plough Lane last week. Tomorrow's second leg will be broadcast live and for free on the Chelsea Official App and website, and begins at 7pm local time (6pm in the UK). Bompastor will be back in the Blues dugout after serving a one-match suspension last week, and ahead of the game in Spain, she delivered the latest team news and outlined the mentality with which her side must approach the game. 'The update for this game is that Erin (Cuthbert), Nat (Nathalie Bjorn), Mayra (Ramirez) and Manaka (Matsukubo) are not available,' she said. 'I think for us, we need to approach the game as if it were 0-0. I have enough experience in football to know anything can happen. 'We have a really good team, and the only thing that will stop us from achieving our goal is if we become complacent and we don't approach the game with the right mindset. 'I think that's what makes the difference between the best teams and the good teams. For me, that's really important, and I will probably mention something to the players before the game tomorrow.' news.title: Tosin Adarabioyo departs on permanent transfer

news.title: Transfer deadline day 2026: Everything you need to know
news.body_en: Transfer Deadline Day has arrived. Here are the key dates, timings and regulations as the summer window draws to a close, plus a recap of Chelsea’s business so far. The 2026 summer transfer window in England closes at 11pm UK time on Tuesday 1 September 2026. The window, which opened on Monday 15 June, has returned to the traditional 11pm deadline following last summer’s earlier finish. The major European leagues also close their windows on Tuesday 1 September. Clubs in the Bundesliga, Serie A and Ligue 1 have until 7pm UK time to complete their business. The window in Spain remains open until 11pm UK time. Players can still leave English clubs after the Premier League window shuts if the destination country’s registration period remains open. Clubs in the Netherlands and Major League Soccer can sign players until Wednesday 2 September. The Scottish window closes at 5pm on Thursday 3 September, with Austria and Belgium also open that day. The deadline in Turkey is Friday 4 September, while clubs in Mexico have until 11 September and those in Portugal until 15 September. The Saudi Arabian window remains open until 12 October. Unattached players can also be signed after the deadline, subject to the relevant competition’s registration and squad-list rules. If two clubs reach an agreement shortly before 11pm, they can submit a deal sheet to the Premier League confirming the transfer. That provides an additional two hours to complete and submit the remaining documentation. As a result, transfers may still be formally completed or announced after the window has closed. Premier League clubs can make unrestricted changes to their squad lists while the transfer window remains open. After the deadline, each club submits a squad containing no more than 25 senior players. No more than 17 of those players can be non-homegrown, with the remaining places reserved for homegrown players. A homegrown player, irrespective of nationality, is somebody who was registered with a club affiliated to the Football Association or Football Association of Wales for three entire seasons or 36 months before turning 21, or before the end of the season in which they turned 21. Players under-21 do not count towards the 25-player limit and remain eligible to play in the Premier League. For the 2026/27 season, that applies to players born on or after 1 January 2005. Marco Palestra became our first recruit of the summer, arriving from Atalanta at the beginning of July. Geovany Quenda and Emmanuel Emegha also officially joined the Blues following agreements reached in previous windows. Morgan Rogers completed a move from Aston Villa and Maxence Lacroix made the short journey across London from Crystal Palace. Danny Welbeck joined from Brighton and Hove Albion, while Jordan Henderson arrived after leaving Brentford. Further additions included Valentin Barco from Strasbourg, Pep Chavarria from Rayo Vallecano and World Cup-winning goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez from Aston Villa. Dastan Satpayev completed his transfer following his 18th birthday before joining Burnley on loan for the season. Youngsters Harrison Bettoni and Alfie Osborne also arrived from Wigan Athletic and Hearts, respectively.
